prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: offshore-wind acceptance/O&M/refurbishment/decommissioning;external-grid/unrelated-ports excluded;reporting active. Aliases: Glassfin=Turbine Controller;Morrowick=Offshore Substation;Pale Lantern=Weather Service;Juniper Vale=SCADA Gateway;Thistle Crown=Maintenance Planning Engine;Amber Quay=Shore Control Room;Kestrel Bay=Crew Transfer Vessel;Sable Orchard=Fleet Dispatch Console;Mosslight=Warehouse System;Copper Finch=Metocean Buoy;Quiet Harbor=Cybersecurity Gateway;Blue Granite=Vessel AIS Receiver;Larkspur=Blade Inspection Drone;Redoubt=Work Permit Portal;Foxglove=Emergency Generator;Wildmere=Grid Interface Relay. Elements: Pitch System;Converter Cabinet;Nacelle Condition Monitor;Rotor Brake Unit;Turbine Sensor Bus;Main Transformer;Export Cable Monitor;Daughter Craft;Service Operations Vessel;Helideck;North Access Scanner;South Access Scanner;Personnel Tracking Console;Spares Hub;Operations Radio Console. Actors: SCADA Engineer;technical reviewers;Electrical Technician;Control Engineer;Grid Dispatcher;Substation Operator;Blade Specialist;Field Supervisor;Marine Coordinator;Duty Planner;Vessel Master;Weather Analyst;Storekeeper;Port Agent;Rescue Coordinator;HSE Officer. Retain source/timestamp/turbine-ID;validate range/freshness/alignment/consistency. Control Engineer evaluates corroboration/severity/persistence/impact,reassesses

New part:
S333: A change in equipment condition, task scope, or operating constraint requires the Field Supervisor to pause work and reassess the authorization.
S334: The Duty Planner coordinates any revised work window with the relevant operational roles before the permit is amended.
S335: The Field Supervisor confirms that tools, temporary connections, and personnel are clear before requesting isolation removal.
S336: The Electrical Technician checks that the work area is ready for restoration and reports any outstanding defects or restrictions.
S337: The Substation Operator removes isolations only under the approved switching process and records each restoration action.
S338: The Control Engineer reviews the restored equipment state and confirms that required operational checks are complete.
S339: The Shore Control Room retains the permit status, isolation history, test results, and restoration decision for operational review.
S340: The Duty Planner closes the work authorization after the Field Supervisor confirms completion or formally records any remaining work.
S341: Equipment returns to service only when operating personnel accept the restored condition and any applicable restrictions are communicated.
S342: The Substation Operator maintains the Offshore Substation within approved operating limits and follows current switching instructions.
S343: At the start of each shift, the operator reviews alarms, active restrictions, equipment status, and handover notes.
S344: Routine rounds cover room temperature, ventilation, water ingress, lighting, access control, and visible signs of damage.
S345: The operator checks Main Transformer temperatures, cooling equipment, oil indications, and abnormal noise against established limits.
S346: The Export Cable Monitor is reviewed for trends or alarms that require escalation to the Control Engineer.
S347: The Grid Interface Relay is checked for healthy indications and consistency with the approved grid operating state.
S348: The SCADA Gateway displays are compared with local indications when equipment status is uncertain.
S349: The Control Engineer investigates unexplained discrepancies before operating personnel rely on remote indications.
S350: The Work Permit Portal is checked to confirm that active work authorizations and isolation boundaries remain current.
S351: The operator verifies that personnel access records are consistent with the planned work and current site occupancy.
S352: The Fire Detection Panel is checked for healthy status, active faults, and unobstructed access to response equipment.
S353: The Emergency Generator produces the Start Test Trace during its scheduled functional test.
S354: The operator confirms fuel level, starting battery condition, ventilation, and readiness of the Emergency Generator for loss of normal supply.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
